content: I am planning today to do some file reorganization of the IEANTN project, which currently consists of about two dozen files sitting in the top level PrimeNumberTheoremAnd directory for Lean files. I will create an IEANTN subdirectory, and then each paper in turn gets a subdirectory of that, with the Lean files associated to those papers moved into those folders. This was previously rather tedious due to the need to update imports, blueprint, etc. but I have now figured out how to get an AI agent to do all the grunt work (and check that both the Lean and the blueprint continue to build properly afterwards), so this has now become feasible. There may be a small amount of disruption for anyone currently working on an IEANTN task, but I believe git is pretty good at handling moving file locations (apart from import header edits, I am not planning any further refactoring). The main cost should be that the project may need to be rebuilt after the refactor.

The refactor is now complete and merged. As far as I can tell, there were no issues with CI etc., but please do let me know if there were disruptions on local repositories. I know this was a somewhat major refactor (44 files moved), but the logistical costs of doing so were only going to increase as the project grew, so I felt it was time to "rip off the band-aid".
